artifacts.description: RMSD (Angstrom) over the trajectory for the CORE domain, computed on alpha-carbon atoms of the 'name CA' AtomGroup with the AtomGroup-based RMSD class.
artifacts.source_evidence: The section 'RMSD of an AtomGroup with multiple selections' interprets this CORE-domain RMSD as a result and plots it ('ax = df.plot(x=Frame, y=CORE...)'). The variable is the DataFrame 'df' built from R.results.rmsd after R = rms.RMSD(ca, ca, select=CORE, ref_frame=0); R.run().

artifacts.description: Mass-weighted RMSD over the trajectory for C-alphas and the CORE, LID and NMP domains.
artifacts.source_evidence: The 'Weighted RMSD of a trajectory - Mass' section presents this table and plot as its outcome (df_mass built from R_mass.results.rmsd; the notebook notes the plot looks largely the same as the unweighted case). 'df_mass' exists at completion.

artifacts.description: RMSD over the trajectory weighted by residue numbers for C-alphas and the CORE, LID and NMP domains.
artifacts.source_evidence: The 'Custom weights' section interprets this result scientifically ('the NMP domain has much higher RMSD than before... residues later in the CORE domain do not seem to contribute significantly'). 'df_charge' is built from R_charge.results.rmsd and exists at completion.

excluded_outputs: Backbone-wide trajectory RMSD with Backbone/CORE/LID/NMP group selections (first rms.RMSD run and its DataFrame): the notebook plots and interprets it, but both the variable R and df are overwritten by the later alpha-carbon analysis, so the values no longer exist at script completion and cannot be exported without rerunning computation.

Single RMSD between open (CRD) and closed (DCD) backbone conformations: computed as a standalone unnamed expression in the 'RMSD between two sets of coordinates' section; capturing it would require assigning a new variable to a previously unnamed expression, which is not permitted. Its value is not recoverable at completion.
explanation: The notebook's terminal scientific results are the three RMSD-versus-frame tables that the narrative interprets and plots: the alpha-carbon CORE-domain RMSD (df, still holding the CA/CORE analysis at completion), the mass-weighted RMSD (df_mass), and the residue-number-weighted RMSD (df_charge). All three exist as named pandas DataFrames at the end of the script. The appended export code only writes these existing DataFrames to CSV files under /work/outputs; it performs no new scientific computation. The earlier backbone-wide trajectory RMSD (R, df with Backbone/CORE/LID/NMP) and the single open-vs-closed rms.rmsd value are excluded because they no longer exist at completion (the first) or were never assigned to a variable (the second).
export_code:
# --- Export of terminal scientific results ---
# Save the existing RMSD result tables produced by the original script.
import os

_output_dir = "/work/outputs"
os.makedirs(_output_dir, exist_ok=True)

df.to_csv(os.path.join(_output_dir, "rmsd_ca_core_domain.csv"), index=False)
df_mass.to_csv(os.path.join(_output_dir, "rmsd_mass_weighted.csv"), index=False)
df_charge.to_csv(os.path.join(_output_dir, "rmsd_resid_weighted.csv"), index=False)
